title: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

sense.text:
“And that servant, which knew his lord’s will, and prepared not himself, neither did according to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes.” The lord’s will is the laws of God. The servant knew the laws of God and did not prepare himself.

Preparing yourself is measuring yourself against the Bible. The Bible is the measuring barometer we look at to see whether we are pairing ourselves off right with God. If we are honest and examine ourselves, in many cases we are not; if Christ came back right now, many of us ain’t right, we ain’t ready. Preparing comes with actually opening the book, reading it for what it says, and doing what it says.

That is why we stand to a higher accountability. Much is given to us, the wisdom to instruct the people, so we had better live it or we are going to get beat with many stripes. Because judgment is not executed speedily, some are under the delusion that they will skate away from the judgment of God. It is imperative that we live up to what we say.

“But he that knew not, and did commit things worthy of stripes, shall be beaten with few stripes.” Some don’t know, or don’t know as much, and they get fewer stripes. So judgments are not always the same for the same infraction. A brother who fornicated was put out; a sister who had been with her husband more than ten years, was in the truth only a few months, slept with him and came and confessed it heartbroken, was not put out. Not much was expected of her yet, she was contrite, and putting her out would not have helped her grow. People say that’s not fair. Yes, it is, and mind your business. But when you are an officer or a captain, that we are not hearing. That doesn’t mean go do it: there is still a God to answer to for what you do to his body.

“For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required.” We understand the will of God. That is much given to us: we have the keys to the kingdom of heaven, when people live a whole life and never understand the will of God. They think saying Hail Mary or singing gospel songs will get them into the kingdom holding hands with Jesus, not knowing that believing is an action word. The witchcraft of Christianity has fried people’s minds. Much was given to us, so much more is required. As you move up in rank the road gets narrower and narrower, till you have to walk blameless.

“And to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.” Brothers complain that they have this office and that office. Maybe it’s because you are really good at what you do that people keep turning to you. If you can’t be used, you’re useless. Among upper leadership all phones are on twenty-four hours a day, because there is so much going on throughout Israel all over the world. You want to grow in wisdom, but much is given, much is required, and you will fulfil a lot more offices.

So we have to walk right: put away the childish things, put away the lust and the things that destroy men, and stay focused on the work at hand. The time is short and the world is watching. If the offense comes, don’t let it come through you or me or any one of us.

precepts.why:
“I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” God defines what his will is: his will is his law. The will of God for us is that we keep the commandments.

So when Luke 12:47 speaks of the servant “which knew his lord’s will”, it is the servant which knew the laws of God, and prepared not himself to do them. That servant shall be beaten with many stripes.

sense.text:
“Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.” Look at how it opens: “when there were gathered together an innumerable multitude of people”. The masses were coming to hear the word of God, so many they were trampling each other trying to get to it. That is when he said to his disciples first of all, beware of walking as a hypocrite.

The people are hungry for the word, so set a right example for them. Be careful how you move, because you will run them off. They will say all these guys are hypocrites, they don’t live what they tell us to do. We cannot be those guys. A teacher cannot sit up here giving scriptures while plotting on sexing one of the sisters, robbing you, or selling drugs; it changes how he is viewed, and much is given, much is required. Before Christ got to much is given in verse 48, the first thing he said at the top of the chapter was beware of the leaven of hypocrisy, before it erodes you.

“For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed; neither hid, that shall not be known.” You are going to be revealed. You are not going to get hid in this life or the world to come. You are not going to get away with it, so be mindful of that.

“Whatsoever ye have spoken in darkness shall be heard in the light”. If you are trying to creep in the darkness, it is going to be proclaimed upon the housetops. Do you want to be the one through whom the offense to this gospel comes? No.

“Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.” The people are coming in to learn, and you are the teacher. When the people come, money comes. People help the body and buy into the system, and they trust that these are the mouthpiece of God. Beware that you get caught up in covetousness.

What a man possesses doesn’t make him who he is. Be careful of the leaven of hypocrisy, be careful of covetousness, be the example you profess you are, and don’t let the riches of this world destroy your mind.

People coming in have had enough of the pastor robbing them: they pay their tithes every week and see the pastor with the plane, the jet, the nice car. When they come here and see men professing to be men of the Lord, they must see that change. We build schools all over the world; that isn’t the machine we run. We are about building Christ’s kingdom, and we hold jobs; none of us is living off the body.

“The life is more than meat, and the body is more than raiment.” Life is more than what you have to eat and the clothes you have to wear. “Consider the ravens: for they neither sow nor reap; which neither have storehouse nor barn; and God feedeth them”. They are taken care of.

This must be a big point he is emphasizing to the twelve. People are coming in, and in Acts 2 they brought money. He is saying, be careful of covetousness, because you are going to see finances come in. Life does not consist of that. As the raven does not sow nor reap and the Lord provides for him, don’t get distracted chasing after riches, because it will lead you away from me.

“But rather seek ye the kingdom of God; and all these things shall be added unto you.” Seek doing my work, leading the people to me. He is charging them with a great mission, to teach the people how to serve God.

We have watched in the past how covetousness almost ripped this congregation apart: chasing behind riches, dealing deceitfully, walking in hypocrisy, lying, murmuring. Murmuring is witchcraft, because it is altering the way you think about a person. Don’t ever come to me murmuring, because I’m going to talk about you openly.

“Fear not, little flock; for it is your Father’s good pleasure to give you the kingdom.” It is God’s good pleasure; he wants us to have it. So don’t get distracted from what he is calling you for. Opening our eyes to this truth is a great gift. There is no greater gift we can ever receive in this world than to know the word of God and have the opportunity to teach it. Now we just have to live it and be it, the true inner man and the true inner woman moving right. Then God will send the people in, and we can lead them.

When God says he wants to give us the kingdom, and not them, he is saying we are special to him. That is why he gives us wisdom. But he requires something back in return, which is fair.

“Sell that ye have, and give alms”. That doesn’t mean sell your house and be homeless; use sense. Remember, a man’s life does not consist of the abundance of things. You are trying to hoard riches on this side, with three or four cars and five or six homes, excess things, while the ministry is lacking.

“For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.” Whatever is important to you is where your mind will be, and our minds should be attentive to this work, because it is the Father’s good pleasure to give us the kingdom.

precepts.why:
“Where are the benefits that I have done for you? when ye were hungry and thirsty in the wilderness, did ye not cry unto me”. They cried, “Why hast thou brought us into this wilderness to kill us? it had been better for us to have served the Egyptians”. “Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so ye did eat angels’ bread.” That must mean we are special to him: when we cried, he said, I’m going to feed you, because you are special to me.

So God is saying, where are my benefits now? Where is the comeback? I chose you to be the people for me; now you have to give me something back. “When ye were thirsty, did I not cleave the rock”, “I cast out the Canaanites, the Pherezites, and the Philistines, before you: what shall I yet do more for you? saith the Lord.” I have done it all. Even when they were “blaspheming my name, I gave you not fire for your blasphemies, but cast a tree in the water, and made the river sweet.” Because you are special to me, I fed you and gave you water to drink.

Then: “What shall I do unto thee, O Jacob? thou, Juda, wouldest not obey me: I will turn me to other nations”. That is us still. “Seeing ye have forsaken me, I will forsake you also”. Because you forsake me, I am going to forsake you too.

So it is with leaders now. I have given you these benefits and charged you to be over my people, to lead the people to me, and you are going to take their money and use them? You are going to walk in hypocrisy and deceive the people? Many stripes you are going to receive. You cannot be in a leadership role, from a soldier on up, and move like that. We want a different program: we are about reaching God’s people sincerely, and when we are in error we correct it among us. The Lord said, where’s my benefits?

sense.text: “I wisdom dwell with prudence”, “The fear of the Lord is to hate evil”, “Counsel is mine, and sound wisdom: I am understanding; I have strength.” Wisdom is speaking.

“By me kings reign, and princes decree justice.” By wisdom leaders reign, and a prince decrees justice. That is what we are about.

For the other camps and brothers who want to understand the success of Israel United in Christ: we are sincere about keeping these commandments and enforcing them among the children of Israel, on top of believing on the Lord and saviour, the black Messiah. That is what brings the masses in, because the people see these guys are moving correctly. Some camps smoke weed, some have multiple wives and don’t take care of them, some look like gangsters. We are not doing that.

“I love them that love me; and those that seek me early shall find me.” God is saying, you are special to me, I love you; but where is my benefit? You have to love me back. He chose us first, and now he says, walk worthy of what I called you for. I am making you special and you are making yourself unspecial.

Seek me early: people start looking for God when they are in prison or have a disease. He is saying, I could be found, but you have to seek me early. You can’t wait until you are in a dilemma and then cry for me. You didn’t take advantage of the opportunity of having the one true God; you did whatever you wanted, walked in hypocrisy, and still expect favour from me.

“Riches and honour are with me; yea, durable riches and righteousness.” “My fruit is better than gold”. The riches we are looking for, people think it’s money. No, we need the durable riches, which is wisdom. He is giving it to us, but we are walking in hypocrisy and distracted by covetousness, when a man’s life does not consist of that.

He was telling them that because it wasn’t their kingdom yet. All this is coming to an end, and I am going to destroy it anyway. You are too focused on this world when I have something far better, and you are about to throw that away for this. Now you understand it, so you have no excuse. Much is given; stand in that space and be it, or get ready to get beat.

precepts.why:
“Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom; teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.” That is what we are supposed to do, with the word dwelling in us richly.

So the riches and honour that are with wisdom in Proverbs 8 are not money. They are the word of Christ dwelling in you richly in all wisdom: the durable riches.

sense.text:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: the Lord thy God hath chosen thee to be a special people unto himself, above all people that are upon the face of the earth.” He chose us to be special unto him, set apart from everybody else. We read it a thousand times, but it never gets old.

The laws of God are our constitution, and they are what makes us holy, special and set apart. The word of God has no power unless you activate it, and the only way to activate it is to do what it says. Otherwise it is just words on a page. The word is alive when you let it live through you by your actions. You become the living example of what it means to be a holy people. That is why the nations say, what a wise and understanding people: they see our actions.

At the big events in the arenas they say, five thousand black people and nobody smoking weed, no fights breaking out? How are they so organized? How can they mobilize a few thousand men, put them on the street, then break down and file back in, and the place is clean? That is the word of God working through us. There is a standard we live by, because we are gods on the earth.

So there has to be something that makes us different from the world and the churches, and we know what it is: the laws of God. Don’t walk in hypocrisy and let go of what he is giving you; it is what will make you shine bright and obtain the kingdom. Be that living example to the people.

“The Lord did not set his love upon you, nor choose you, because ye were more in number than any people; for ye were the fewest of all people”. It wasn’t numbers. We were the fewest, but we were special.

“But because the Lord loved you”. For no other reason: he loved us. He said, I like this lot right here, this is my favourite lot. Thank you, Lord, for choosing us. It could have been worse; I could have woke up the owner of China Buffet. For whatever reason the Lord chose me. They called me nigger; he called me Israelite. You are special to me and I love you. Well, Lord, I love you back; show me where I am wrong so I can fix it and live honestly in this. That is for all of us, but especially for leadership, because we are the ones teaching the masses, and it has to be consistent.

He loved us “and because he would keep the oath which he had sworn unto your fathers”, and brought us out of the house of bondmen.

“The faithful God, which keepeth covenant and mercy with them that love him and keep his commandments to a thousand generations”. He is a faithful God to those that keep his commandments and love him back.

“And repayeth them that hate him to their face, to destroy them”. If you don’t return his benefits, you are telling him you hate him. He gave you charge to lead and teach the people, and you take advantage of them. Leaders using their position to beguile the sisters into sex, to keep them in a filthy mindset, or to take advantage of people for money: God is going to judge you. You pass off conversations like you are counselling them while you are trying to line them up. You hate God and you hate his people.

Let the sisters get counsel from sisters. When you give counsel, make sure it is beneficial to them, what God wants them to hear, not your own wants and lust.

Sisters come into IUIC and say the leaders at the camp they came from immediately tried to get their number. Here they are sent to the sisters to be built up. There are processes and contingencies in place, because Israel is coming in and everyone is battling their own lust. A man will cleave to his like, so examine yourself: are you coming in cleaving to the old man or the old woman, or striving to reach the example of our forefathers, so that others can be exhorted by your actions behind the scenes?

precepts.why: “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good.” What makes us a holy people? The law is holy. So if we are a holy people, we are supposed to be a law-abiding people. The laws of God being applied is what makes us holy and special.

“But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.” As in the time of Rome, so in this captivity: our people are lost, with no shepherd, confused. Not only have the people of the world taken advantage of us, but our own people take advantage too, getting preeminence.

As Christ went out teaching and healing, he saw his people had fainted. They were in the streets, they didn’t worship their God, and their own leaders were taking advantage of them. We as leaders are moved by the same thing: our people are afflicted, they have no leaders, and they are looking for a shepherd, which is ultimately Christ.

So instead of benefiting ourselves, we see the decayed state of our people and deny ourselves: to hell with the riches, to hell with the women and having sex. We will do whatever it takes to rebuild our nation, so that we benefit each other and have one shepherd to rule over us. That is the spirit the Lord has put in us, and those are the ones standing in these last days, speaking with authority and showing our people, let’s move according to this holy word and restore this nation.

“There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.” You can’t be a hypocrite, especially in a leadership position. Look at the other camps: they are supposed to be leading the people, but their mind is on the riches, or on how many bodies they can notch on their belt.

What makes you wise? Keeping the commandments. Those leaders know they are Israel, God’s chosen people, supposed to keep the laws. But because of bad intentions, covetousness, their god being money and power to persuade the people, they are unprofitable to themselves. And nothing will be hid: everything done will be revealed in time.

sense.text: “For God is not the author of confusion, but of peace”. When a sister goes to another man for understanding instead of her husband, it causes confusion.

“And if they will learn any thing, let them ask their husbands at home”. She may not understand something and want clarity. Her husband, her lord, should be the one she goes to for wisdom and understanding, not another man. We see through a glass darkly; there are things we know and things we don’t. If her husband doesn’t know, he comes and gets understanding.

You don’t want to give another man power over your house, where she says, well, so-and-so bishop or deacon or captain said it. No man wants to hear that, and some men who are leaders will come in and beguile your wife. So it is not for any of you brothers to be instructing another man’s wife in the scriptures, or investigating what another man’s wife or daughters know. That isn’t your business.

“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness”. God’s image is the greatest image there is, and he made man after it, with attributes and a look like his. That is why he said you are special: I am mirroring you after me. And after giving you his image, “let them have dominion”: he gave us power and rulership.

“So God created man in his own image”, “And God blessed them”. God blessed us with his image and with dominion.

So if we try to change that image or skirt around the laws of God, we betray it. We are at the lowest state right now because we sinned against God. But I don’t want to share power with any nation. This isn’t all-inclusive, voting and holding hands. I want it all or none, and I will stay in this state as long as it takes until God puts us back in our rightful state.

precepts.why:
“And the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” The blessing didn’t end with his image and dominion. He blessed us with the breath of life, which is wisdom, and then we were activated. The word of God has to activate your life; he gave us laws to govern us so we can be that special people, or we would be just like every other nation.

How can I be made in his image and likeness and given the breath of life, which is wisdom, and walk in hypocrisy, worried about the riches of this world, when he has something better for me? We are where we are because we didn’t see the benefit of having him over us. God said, are you people stupid? I gave you the all and that still isn’t good enough? You are going to be led away by a vagina, which I made? Money, riches and cars are greater than what I am giving you? When you put it in that perspective: no, Lord.

sense.text:
“For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me: for in her is an understanding spirit”. With wisdom comes an understanding spirit. That is why we understand the Bible. People ask, how do you do that, you’ve got a scripture for everything you say? That is wisdom having free course through our lives.

“Holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled, plain”. Tether yourself to wisdom.

“Kind to man”: wisdom is kind to the man that loves wisdom. “Steadfast, sure”: reliable, durable. “Free from care”: free from worry and stress, free from the cares of this world. Because you are applying it, you are not subject to the riches of the world. God said beware of covetousness; that is wisdom, so I am going to beware of it and not entertain it.

“Having all power, overseeing all things”. Wisdom oversees all things, so it is in our best interest to be paired with wisdom, that we can see clearly.

“she passeth and goeth through all things by reason of her pureness.” Because wisdom is pure and undefiled, if we tether to it, everything becomes plain to us. We would understand there is no way to be close to God and be a special people while moving in hypocrisy, or sinning unchecked and thinking we will receive the kingdom. Wisdom makes that plain.

The Lord needs us to be like this, so that when the masses come they see the right example: these are really the guys, look at their order. A sister came into the truth because she saw the camp in the streets and none of the brothers tried to talk to her. She was used to men trying to talk to her, and that was enough to say, something is different here.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty”. Influence means to mould you. Wisdom flows down from the Almighty, and if it is influencing you, you are tethered to God. Or something else is influencing you: covetousness, lust, whatever it might be.

“Therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” Nothing defiled can fall into wisdom, so tether yourself to it, because it comes down from God, and you are safe. That was the breath he gave us in Genesis 2. We breathed it in and then looked at what everybody else was doing. God gave us the best thing we could ever have, and something else was able to influence us and direct us away from him. Where’s my benefits?

“For she is the brightness of the everlasting light, the unspotted mirror of the power of God, and the image of his goodness.” Wisdom is the unspotted mirror; to keep yourself unspotted, tether yourself to God, because wisdom flows down from him.

“She maketh all things new”. Wisdom flows down from God to you; you come into this truth not knowing any better, you apply it, and you become new. You can’t keep on doing the same thing.

“And in all ages entering into holy souls, she maketh them friends of God, and prophets.” Wisdom enters into holy souls and dwells there, but it cannot dwell in a body subject to sin, hypocrisy, covetousness or hatred. When you move like that you say absurd things, like the mark of the beast is COVID.

You are made new, made a friend of God and a prophet, and then you go out and raise up God’s children. That is why he said you can’t walk in hypocrisy: we are charged with that. Much is given, much is required.

precepts.why:
“And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word, And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.” The cares of the world, the riches, the lust and other things deceive you.

Wisdom is “free from care”: free from these cares. With wisdom you are not going to be subject to the riches of the world. A man’s life does not consist in the abundance of things.

“Let us labour therefore to enter into that rest, lest any man fall after the same example of unbelief.” If we believe, we are tethered with God and following wisdom, which is pure, steadfast and sure, and we enter into that rest.

“For the word of God is quick, and powerful”: we just read in Wisdom of Solomon that wisdom is quick, and that she is the breath of the power of God. The power of God is the word of God; it is wisdom. It is “a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart.” Sin begins in the intents of the heart.

So we want that pure influence, that what guides and directs our minds is the word of God. There should be something in all of us that says, I can’t do that, it’s wrong. If we turn aside from that, we are hypocrites who don’t really believe, and God chose us to give us wisdom and we are not moving like those people.

“The law of the Lord is perfect, converting the soul: the testimony of the Lord is sure, making wise the simple.” We were once simple, but wisdom is now in us, making us wise.

“The statutes of the Lord are right, rejoicing the heart: the commandment of the Lord is pure, enlightening the eyes.” That pure influence of Wisdom of Solomon 7:25 is the statutes, the laws of God. With our eyes enlightened we see clearly, and the Lord has converted us. We are new; remember that word.

“And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.” When the word of God deals with you, you change into another man. But if you are still living that old man and still doing the same things, the Lord says, I’m going to beat you with many stripes, because I gave you something and you weren’t listening.

Beaten with many stripes isn’t a little pow-pow and that’s it. Many in that day will say Lord, Lord, and he is going to say, I don’t know you.

“For of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.” What comes out of his mouth is what is in him. “And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?” You hear it, you acknowledge it, you know it, and you don’t do it.

He that “heareth my sayings, and doeth them” is like a man who “laid the foundation on a rock”, and the stream “could not shake it”. The one built on Christ, the rock, is the one applying it, and that is what strengthens us to endure when tribulations come. Wisdom teaches us that plainly. “But he that heareth, and doeth not” built without a foundation, “and immediately it fell”.

In that day men will say, Lord, Lord. You were out on the street teaching, but you were a hypocrite and weren’t living it. Brothers come wanting to understand deep prophecies; first let’s get you off Pornhub. Why are you in Revelation trying to understand archangels? You know prophecy, but you don’t know you yet. Learn you, so you can live it and instruct the people wisely how to serve God.

“Pure religion and undefiled before God and the Father is this, To visit the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep himself unspotted from the world.” The people come in afflicted in the mind, and you are too busy trying to bag the chick. She came out of the world, and instead of leading her to God you are trying to sleep with her.

If we want to know how to keep ourselves unspotted, as wisdom is “the unspotted mirror of the power of God”, tether yourself to God, because wisdom flows down from him.

“Be as a father unto the fatherless, and instead of an husband unto their mother: so shalt thou be as the son of the most High”. When we put our interests over the Lord’s interests, it distances us from him; when we put his interests over ours, it brings us closer to the heavenly Father.

The wrong mindset says, what can I do to this sister? instead of, what can I do for this young man to build him up? Bishop Nathanyel says it is easier to build up a child than to fix a broken old man, and that broken old man says, how can I take advantage of this single mother?

If you are going opposite of that, looking at a sister with lustful eyes to get in her pants or take advantage of her, you cannot be the son of the most High, and wisdom cannot dwell in you. That goes right back to Wisdom of Solomon 7:27: wisdom enters into holy souls and makes them friends of God.

“Can the children of the bridechamber mourn, as long as the bridegroom is with them? but the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, and then shall they fast.” While Christ was with them he was teaching them. When he was gone they would have to have wisdom with them, because he would not be there to teach them. He leaves a comforter to guide them, and there would come a famine of the word.

To take in this word you have to become like a child. You can’t be set in your ways, like some old people you can’t tell anything. “Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break”, “but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved.” New is the word. You can’t put this wisdom into a person who won’t be taught. Tell the Christians Jesus will judge them for eating pork, or that they can’t be married to an Edomite wife, or can’t be gay, and it is too much for them. You have to be converted and become new to accept this wisdom.

After the famine, God said the hour has come when he sends the prophets back on the earth. Those prophets became new men, friends of God and prophets, because they became new creatures who could digest the word and understand the will of God. And now you want to walk as a hypocrite? We have to be the image of God in all things, a nation of men and women that make the next generation better than us, until we become unstoppable.

sense.text: “We then, as workers together with him, beseech you also that ye receive not the grace of God in vain.” We are workers together with him, and we beg that you don’t receive this word in vain: that it becomes profitable to you, that you become prophets of God, that the women bear our prophets back on the earth and our daughters are righteous.

“Behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.” The day of salvation is at hand. This is the time to be right, to be the ambassadors of God. This is what he died for, to give us the opportunity. Are we going to waste it?

“Giving no offence in any thing, that the ministry be not blamed”. Don’t be the setback to the ministry: one of us out there selling drugs, one a murderer, one a thief. Being called as ambassadors, don’t be that brother.

“But in all things approving ourselves as the ministers of God, in much patience, in afflictions, in necessities, in distresses, In stripes, in imprisonments”. This is the cost of being a minister of God.

“By the word of truth, by the power of God, by the armour of righteousness on the right hand and on the left”. We are girded with the word of God on our right hand and left. If we are girded with this wisdom as ambassadors of God, our conversation is the word of God, and our affiliation is with believers like us. This is our life. I don’t have another life; if I wasn’t doing this, I wouldn’t know what to do or whom to call. If you have something else you can do outside of this, you ain’t in the truth.

“Be ye not unequally yoked together with unbelievers”. It is unequal to be with them because you are not of their sort. You are tethered to God and his wisdom, and a prophet; if you are moving with unbelievers doing unbeliever stuff, you are a hypocrite, you don’t really believe, you are faking it.

“For what fellowship hath righteousness with unrighteousness? and what communion hath light with darkness?” None. Our fellowship is with believers doing the will of God. “And what concord hath Christ with Belial? or what part hath he that believeth with an infidel?” If your best friend is somebody in the world, you ain’t in the truth, brothers and sisters alike. You just put on the purple and the fringes. You tell me your friend just finished celebrating Christmas and you are proud of it: you don’t believe. If you have a life outside of this, your life ain’t in here.

precepts.why:
“Now then we are ambassadors for Christ, as though God did beseech you by us”. We are ambassadors and prophets for Christ. God is calling the people by using us. That means we are special and set apart: Lord, why did you choose me to call your people to you?

“For he hath made him to be sin for us, who knew no sin; that we might be made the righteousness of God in him.” He made him to bear our sins. Did God send his son to die so we could continue sinning in hypocrisy? I sent Christ down to die for your sins, I gave you the laws of God, I made you my friends, prophets and ambassadors, and you want to be a hypocrite? Not many stripes for you: you have to die.

So we, as workers together with him, beseech the people not to receive the grace of God in vain.

sense.text: “Let us now praise famous men”, “Such as did bear rule in their kingdoms, men renowned for their power, giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring prophecies”. Men of renown, tied to God, using wisdom to give understanding, and understanding prophecy. The prophecy now is that the time is short: it is coming to an end, so get ready and don’t get caught slipping.

“Leaders of the people by their counsels, and by their knowledge of learning meet for the people, wise and eloquent are their instructions”. “Such as found out musical tunes, and recited verses in writing”: spiritual songs and psalms.

“Rich men furnished with ability”. When you read rich you think money. No: these are rich in the word of God, as in Colossians, the word dwelling richly. Furnished with the ability to give counsel and understanding.

“All these were honoured in their generations, and were the glory of their times.” We want to be the glory of this time, that when our name is spoken they say, that was a man of understanding. The men named were not living in hypocrisy; some of them fell off, but they got right with God.

“There be of them, that have left a name behind them”, and some “have no memorial”. That doesn’t mean they didn’t do mighty works; you couldn’t name them all, just as in this time there will be a hundred and forty-four thousand and a multitude no man can number. “But these were merciful men, whose righteousness hath not been forgotten.” Not forgotten by God.

“With their seed shall continually remain a good inheritance, and their children are within the covenant.” For us as men and fathers, our legacy is our children, who continue this mission when we are gone, so you can see who that man was through his child and grandchild. In many of our lives we are the first generation in this truth. We don’t want to come into the truth, die, and have our kids go back to the rodeo, our granddaughter out there twerking in booty shorts. We break that generational curse.

“Their seed standeth fast”, “Their bodies are buried in peace; but their name liveth for evermore.” That is what we want, our name to live for evermore with God.
“The people will tell of their wisdom, and the congregation will shew forth their praise.” Because they instructed the people when the people came in, and didn’t move in hypocrisy and deceit.
“Enoch pleased the Lord, and was translated, being an example of repentance to all generations.” “Noah was found perfect and righteous”. These are the famous men named.
“Abraham was a great father of many people”.
The covenant was established with Isaac, “And made it rest upon the head of Jacob. He acknowledged him in his blessing”.

“Even Moses, beloved of God and men, whose memorial is blessed.” “He made him like to the glorious saints, and magnified him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.” We want to be named among these, to have this legacy and be right with God.

Moses had his faults. He didn’t circumcise, and Zipporah had to do it; he spoke unadvisedly and didn’t see the promised land. But God still chose him and his legacy lived on.
“He exalted Aaron, an holy man like unto him, even his brother, of the tribe of Levi.”

“He gave unto him his commandments, and authority in the statutes of judgments, that he should teach Jacob the testimonies, and inform Israel in his laws.” That is our job: to inform the people of the Lord and teach them the statutes of God. Ladies, you cannot wear that; brothers, you cannot eat that; sisters, cover your head; brothers, rule your house.

This is how they got their fame: instructed in the laws of God, tethered to God with his wisdom, making people new. I want that legacy, to say God used me to make this person new, so at the end I can say I fought a good fight, I kept the faith, I did the work.
“But he made Aaron more honourable, and gave him an heritage”.

“The third in glory is Phinees the son of Eleazar, because he had zeal in the fear of the Lord, and stood up with good courage of heart: when the people were turned back”. When the people were turning back, he contended with them and stood firm for the laws of God. (That is not a call to kill anybody.)

“God give you wisdom in your heart to judge his people in righteousness, that their good things be not abolished, and that their glory may endure for ever.” You can do this for twenty or thirty years, then give up, and everything you did goes away. Then you won’t be the famous man; you will be the example of what not to do.

“Jesus the son a Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God”. He was made a great man for saving the elect of God, “and taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, that he might set Israel in their inheritance.”

“He and Caleb the son of Jephunne, in that they withstood the congregation, and withheld the people from sin, and appeased the wicked murmuring.” The people were unruly, and Joshua and Caleb withstood them and stood firm in the laws of God. This is how you gain your legacy and your name. Much is given, much is required: you are going to go up against the masses with this word, and that is what we are doing now, as the brothers did in Atlanta, standing firm in the word of God.

“The Lord gave strength also unto Caleb, which remained with him unto his old age”. He was old, but still fervent in this word and still stood for the laws of God. There is no expiration and no retirement; retirement is death or the kingdom. Until our dying breath we strive for this truth, in a wheelchair or in your cabin.

“That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” Look at him: he is an example that it is good to follow the Lord. Follow this one; look how the Lord works through him. We want to be that example to the people.

“As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.” “He played with lions as with kids, and with bears as with lambs. Slew he not a giant, when he was yet but young?”
“For he destroyed the enemies on every side”. He did many great works. “With his whole heart he sung songs, and loved him that made him.” But didn’t David sin against God?

“The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” David sinned against God, but he repented, and God took away his sins. This is a famous man, and an example to all of us: some of us err in this truth, but you can recover yourself and still earn a name. You just have to do the work and be sincere.

“But the Lord will never leave off his mercy”, “neither will he abolish the posterity of his elect, and the seed of him that loveth him he will not take away: wherefore he gave a remnant unto Jacob, and out of him a root unto David.”

precepts.why:
After David confessed his sin, what did he do? “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me. Against thee, thee only, have I sinned, and done this evil in thy sight”. “Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean: wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow.”

“Then will I teach transgressors thy ways; and sinners shall be converted unto thee.” Get myself right, and then go teach the people. That is why it is written of the famous men that all Israel might see it is good to follow the Lord: look at my example, it is good to follow the Lord, because in the end the Lord chose me as his friend. So “The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever”.

sense.text: “Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.”

“Who wast ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the Lord’s judgment, before it brake forth into fury”. That is our job, before the decree brings forth the fierce anger of God, as in Zephaniah 3. “And to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.” Our job is to turn our people back to God. What is well pleasing to God is for us to keep his laws and then become the prophets who lead the people back to them. Much is given, much is required of us in our walk as leaders, so we have to be honest.
“Of whom some did that which was pleasing to God, and some multiplied sins.” Some did the laws of God, and some multiplied sins.

precepts.why:
“This is the book of the commandments of God, and the law that endureth for ever: all they that keep it shall come to life; but such as leave it shall die.” “O Israel, happy are we: for things that are pleasing to God are made known unto us.”

What is pleasing to God is his laws. Us keeping the law is what pleases God. So when Ecclesiasticus 48:16 says “some did that which was pleasing to God”, it means some kept the laws of God.

sense.text: “The remembrance of Josias is like the composition of the perfume that is made by the art of the apothecary”. When the apothecary mixed the oils, it was set apart, holy, consecrated, not like anything else. Josias was like that; and if you are not like anything else, you are special.

“He behaved himself uprightly in the conversion of the people, and took away the abominations of iniquity.” As the people were converting back to God, he wasn’t using his position to take advantage of them, handling the word of God deceitfully, or trying to mack the sisters on the side under cover of counsel. He moved uprightly.

Compare the church: Eddie Long, the pastor in the speedos; what did he convert them into? And the people still held him up in that chair afterward. The church is crazy.

“He directed his heart unto the Lord, and in the time of the ungodly he established the worship of God.” In this time of the ungodly we are going to establish the worship of God. That is how you become the famous man: in the midst of all this debauchery we don’t walk in hypocrisy, covetousness or murmuring. We direct the people to God and show them how to live godly, and the nations will say, these are those guys we heard about who were going to come back on the earth.

“All, except David and Ezekias and Josias, were defective: for they forsook the law of the most High, even the kings of Juda failed.” All these men failed. “Therefore he gave their power unto others, and their glory to a strange nation.” That is where the northern kingdom came in. “They burnt the chosen city of the sanctuary, and made the streets desolate, according to the prophecy of Jeremias.”
“And of the twelve prophets let the memorial be blessed, and let their bones flourish again out of their place: for they comforted Jacob, and delivered them by assured hope.”
“How shall we magnify Zorobabel? even he was as a signet on the right hand”.

“And among the elect was Neemias, whose renown is great, who raised up for us the walls that were fallen, and set up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again.” Along with raising up the walls of Jerusalem, he established the laws: you are not going to get our people to shop on the sabbath. These were the men of renown.
“Neither was there a young man born like Joseph, a governor of his brethren, a stay of the people, whose bones were regarded of the Lord.”

“Simon the high priest, the son of Onias, who in his life repaired the house again, and in his days fortified the temple”. These renowned men earned their name by building back, walking in integrity and moving right. Go back through these chapters; there is a lot more in them.

“Let a man so account of us, as of the ministers of Christ, and stewards of the mysteries of God. Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.” In a steward, you have to be found faithful.

“For I think that God hath set forth us the apostles last, as it were appointed to death: for we are made a spectacle unto the world, and to angels, and to men.” This is the cost: we are a spectacle, appointed unto death. Do you want to die as an apostle with the old leaven still living in you, or be found faithful? Lord, Lord, did I not prophesy in your name? I don’t know you. Why run this whole race and not get it?

Much is given, much is required. I have given you understanding; where are my benefits back? Are you playing games, treating this Bible as a joke?

precepts.why: “Purge out therefore the old leaven, that ye may be a new lump, as ye are unleavened. For even Christ our passover is sacrificed for us”. If you want to be a minister of Christ and a steward found faithful, you have to purge out the old leaven inside you. You can’t be moving with old leaven in you. Christ died for our sins, so you have to purge it out.

sense.text:
“Having therefore these promises, dearly beloved, let us cleanse ourselves from all filthiness of the flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.” The promises are that he will be our Father and we his sons and daughters. When you cleanse yourself from all this filthiness, you are new.

We do this in the fear of God, the fear of his judgment. That is why we perfect ourselves.
“Receive us; we have wronged no man, we have corrupted no man, we have defrauded no man.” We are not moving in deceit; we have not defrauded or wronged anybody.

precepts.why: What are “these promises”? “And will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.” But to be his sons and daughters you have to do this: “Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord, and touch not the unclean thing; and I will receive you”. Then you are not giving offense to the ministry, and he can receive you.

“Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”, “behold, all things are become new.” Cleansed from all filthiness, all things are new. Then I will be your Father and you will be my sons and daughters. But you have to come out of this world; you can’t live in hypocrisy.

“Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord, we persuade men”. We know the terror and the fear of God, so we persuade all people to come out of that, because you are going to die in it. Meanwhile you are walking as a hypocrite? Our job is to persuade men because we understand the fear of God, and that is why we cleanse ourselves, “perfecting holiness in the fear of God.”

“For the love of Christ constraineth us”, “that they which live should not henceforth live unto themselves, but unto him which died for them, and rose again.” If we know he died for us and the love of Christ constrains us, we don’t live in deceit. How do we tell the people to come out of the world and touch not the unclean thing, and then not live it ourselves?

God says, you had the understanding of all these things; I gave you a lot of understanding, so I am going to punish you accordingly, because you knew better. How do I know? Because you were profitable to many, but not profitable to yourself.

sense.text:
“The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek”. He has chosen and set all of us apart, all these captains, to preach good tidings unto the meek.

“He hath sent me to bind up the brokenhearted”. Brokenhearted is broken in the mind: suffering the curses, not knowing the will of God. We are set to bind them up.

“To proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all that mourn”. Remember the accepted time of 2 Corinthians 6:2. Our job is to preach good tidings: that if we repent, keep God’s laws in sincerity and endure to the end, he will deliver us, and we will rule again. We were made in his image to rule. We are going to proclaim it.

“To give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness”. We bring joy to them. “They shall build the old wastes, they shall raise up the former desolations”. “The sons of the alien shall be your plowmen and your vinedressers.” “But ye shall be named the Priests of the Lord: men shall call you the Ministers of our God: ye shall eat the riches of the Gentiles”. That is what we are called to do: to bind these people’s minds to God, and we have to do it in sincerity.

precepts.why: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” What do we bind the brokenhearted with? We bind up the testimony and seal the law in the minds of the people, because their minds are broken. We are called to bind them to the laws of God, and to show them why it is good to serve God by our lives as the example. You have to be sincere about it.

“Thus saith the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages”. The acceptable year of Isaiah 61:2 is the acceptable time here. In this acceptable time we heal the broken heart and proclaim liberty to the captives.

“The Lord hath called me from the womb”, “And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” We are supposed to glorify our God in this body.

“Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.” We go to stiffnecked, hardhearted people who refuse to hear the word of God, but we still proclaim the day of the Lord to heal their minds and tell them there is an end to this, and we will rule one day. He formed us from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him”.

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”. It may not appear that we are doing it, but he is still charging us to raise up the children of Israel and bring back the preserved of Israel. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: our job is to bring salvation to the people and lead them back to him. That is a great ministry. And “he shall choose thee”: out of all, he is going to choose us.

“Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.”

“A bruised reed shall he not break”: he is not going to be broken or destroyed. He is the example of how we are supposed to stand, like those in 2 Esdras who stood stiffly for the word of God. We are not going to be broken and we are not going to give out. The word will be in our mouth like fire, and we will teach it till the end comes. One thing we will not do is stop, and what we cannot do is walk in hypocrisy.

sense.text: “For unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: and to whom men have committed much, of him they will ask the more.” The Lord is letting us know that for this gift he imparted to us, he is going to want more from us. The more understanding you have, the more he will require of you, and the more severe the punishment for not doing it.

“Who then is that faithful and wise steward, whom his lord shall make ruler over his household, to give them their portion of meat in due season? Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.” We want the Lord to find us doing this work: the faithful servant, found doing it in sincerity and honesty, without deceit, without guile, without secret sins. Align yourself with the scriptures and be found faithful in that day. That goes for all of us.
